summary: performance lens over drill-transactions-api (22 product path(s), 5a9ff14..a14920d, Codex via the autoreview skill at --max-priority P2): 0 blocking, 2 non-blocking. The functional predicate and pinning flow shown in the diff is largely consistent with the stated contracts, but the new hot path has two concrete production performance defects: its timeout does not stop database work, and every drill loads an entire pinned outline to resolve one node.

non_blocking_findings.summary: [P2] Cancel warehouse statements when the request timeout expires (backend/src/warehouse/drill-transactions.repository.ts:86): `withTimeout` only races the warehouse promise against a timer; it does not cancel either SQL statement.

[P2] Query the requested outline node instead of loading the full snapshot (backend/src/warehouse/statement-outline.repository.ts:14): The new pinned-batch lookup delegates to the generic outline reader, which selects, orders, transfers, and materializes up to 25,000 outline rows.
